Q80301200.label: 2020 Vincentian general election
Q80301200.summary: General elections were held in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines on 5 November 2020. Nomination day was 20 October 2020. The result was a victory for the Unity Labour Party, its fifth in a row; the party won nine of the fifteen seats, gaining one seat.

Q7401616.label: 1989 Saint Kitts and Nevis general election
aliases: Saint Kitts and Nevis general election, 1989
Q7401616.wiki: 1989 Saint Kitts and Nevis general election
Q7401616.summary: General elections were held in Saint Kitts and Nevis on 21 March 1989. The result was a victory for the People's Action Movement (PAM), which won six of the eleven directly-elected seats. The ruling majority coalition of PAM and the Nevis Reformation Party continued as a result of the elections.

mentions.c: Saint Kitts and Nevis: 1989 Saint Kitts and Nevis general election
Saint Kitts and Nevis: 1989 Saint Kitts and Nevis general election

Q887440.label: Gustavo Adolfo Espina Salguero
Q887440.img: Retrato oficial de Vicepresidente Gustavo Adolfo Espina Salguero.jpg
Q887440.summary: Gustavo Adolfo Espina Salguero was a Guatemalan politician who served as vice president from 1991 to 1993 under President Jorge Serrano and later Acting President for 4 days during the 1993 Guatemalan constitutional crisis.

mentions.c: Guatemala: Gustavo Adolfo Espina Salguero takes power

Q5174928.label: 1990 Costa Rican general election
Q5174928.desc: General election held in Costa Rica
Q5174928.summary: General elections were held in Costa Rica on 4 February 1990. Rafael Ángel Calderón Fournier of the Social Christian Unity Party (PUSC) won the presidential election, whilst his party also won the parliamentary election. Voter turnout was 81.8%.

mentions.c: Costa Rica: 1990 Costa Rican general election
Costa Rica: 1990 Costa Rican general election

Q2388624.label: 1932 French legislative election
Q2388624.summary: Legislative elections were held in France on 1 and 8 May 1932 to elect the 15th legislature of the French Third Republic.

Q105556112.label: 2025 Liechtenstein parliamentary election
Q105556112.summary: General elections were held in Liechtenstein on 9 February 2025 to elect the 25 members of the Landtag. The Patriotic Union (VU) won a plurality of 10 seats, while the Progressive Citizens' Party (FBP) won seven, the lowest in its history.

Q18243216.label: Catholic Centre Party
Q18243216.summary: The Portuguese Catholic Centre was a political party in Portugal. Founded in 1915, it won seats in six consecutive elections, before being disbanded in January 1940.

mentions.c: Party of António de Oliveira Salazar (Portugal, 1932–1968)

Q48860816.label: 1948 Czechoslovak presidential election
Q48860816.summary: The 1948 Czechoslovak presidential election took place on 14 June 1948. Klement Gottwald was elected the first Communist president of Czechoslovakia.

Q518800.label: 1987 Italian general election
Q518800.summary: General elections were held in Italy on 14–15 June 1987. This election was the first Italian election in which the distance between the Christian Democrats and the Communists grew significantly instead of decreasing. Two parties that had not previously been in parliament won representation: the Greens with thirteen seats, and the Northern League with two.

Q1648272.label: Party of Democratic Progress
Q1648272.summary: The Party of Democratic Progress is a centre to centre-right Serb political party in Bosnia and Herzegovina founded on 26 September 1999. It is the third-largest party in the Republika Srpska entity.

mentions.c: Party of Mladen Ivanić (Bosnia and Herzegovina, 2014–2015)

Q299152.label: Emil Constantinescu
Q299152.summary: Emil Constantinescu is a Romanian politician and professor, who served as the second President of Romania from 1996 to 2000. After the Romanian Revolution of 1989, Constantinescu became a founding member and vice president of the Civic Alliance (AC). In addition, he also served as the acting president of the Democratic Romanian Anti-Totalitarian Forum, the first associative structure of the democratic opposition in post-1989 Romania, which was later transformed into a centre-right political and electoral alliance known as the Romanian Democratic Convention (CDR).

Q1390224.label: Marģers Skujenieks
Q1390224.img: Marģers Skujenieks, Prime Minister of Latvia. Situational photography.jpg
Q1390224.summary: Marģers Skujenieks held the office of Prime Minister of Latvia twice from 19 December 1926 – 23 January 1928 and 6 December 1931 – 23 March 1933.

Q99015824.label: 2025 Belarusian presidential election
Q99015824.summary: Presidential elections were held in Belarus on 26 January 2025. The president is directly elected to serve a five-year term.

Q110660240.label: 2022 Armenian presidential election
Q110660240.summary: Early presidential elections were held in Armenia on 3 March 2022, following President Armen Sarkissian's resignation on 23 January 2022.

Q2917008.label: 1981 Israeli legislative election
Q2917008.summary: Legislative elections were held in Israel on 30 June 1981 to elect the 120 members of the Knesset. The ruling Likud won one more seat than the opposition Alignment, in line with many polls which had predicted a tight race. Voter turnout was 78.5%, with Likud receiving around ten thousand more than the Alignment.

Q2002064.label: New START
Q2002064.desc: 2010 nuclear arms reduction treaty between the United States and the Russian Federation
Q2002064.img: Obama and Medvedev sign Prague Treaty 2010.jpeg
Q2002064.summary: New START was a nuclear arms reduction treaty between the United States and Russia with the formal name of Measures for the Further Reduction and Limitation of Strategic Offensive Arms. It was signed on 8 April 2010 in Prague, and after ratification it entered into force on 5 February 2011.

mentions.c: United States: Treaty signed: New START

Q59647120.label: 2018 Strasbourg attack
Q59647120.img: Fusillade de Strasbourg, intervention police route de l'hôpital Neudorf, 11 décembre 2018 - 7.jpg
Q59647120.summary: On the evening of 11 December 2018, a terrorist attack occurred in Strasbourg, France, when a man attacked civilians in the city's busy Christkindelsmärik with a revolver and a knife, killing five and wounding 11 before fleeing in a taxi. Authorities called the shooting an act of terrorism.

Q66764432.label: Hurricane Dorian
Q66764432.summary: Hurricane Dorian was an extremely powerful and catastrophic tropical cyclone, which became the most intense on record to strike the Bahamas. It is tied with the 1935 Labor Day hurricane and Hurricane Melissa in 2025 for the strongest landfall in the Atlantic basin in terms of maximum sustained winds.

Q847504.label: Democratic Coalition
Q847504.summary: The Democratic Coalition is a social democratic and social-liberal political party in Hungary. Founded in 2010 by former prime minister Ferenc Gyurcsány as a faction within the Hungarian Socialist Party (MSZP), the Democratic Coalition split from the MSZP on 22 October 2011 and became a separate party. Until the 2026 parliamentary election it had fifteen MPs in the National Assembly, but at those elections it failed to reach the 5% threshold required and so no longer has any representatives there, although it still has two MEPs in the European Parliament.

Q337040.label: George Bernard Dantzig
Q337040.summary: George Bernard Dantzig was an American mathematical scientist who made contributions to industrial engineering, operations research, computer science, economics, and statistics.

Member of: American Academy of Arts and Sciences
